vikram (Finance): Heads-up: starting 2026-06-01 were introducing a "soft overage" protection and a new invoice line-item breakdown. A few reasons: reduce emergency charge disputes, make overages predictable, and surface per-model unit costs on invoices.

vikram (Finance): TL;DR:
- Soft overage protection: auto-apply a one-time grace buffer of $50 or 5% of monthly commit (whichever is lower) to new customers for their first billing month after the policy goes live. This will absorb small unexpected bursts.
- Dispute window shortened: customers must open invoice disputes within 30 days (was 60); finance will still accept good-faith late disputes but they require manager sign-off.
- Invoice detail: invoices will now include per-model and per-route line items (model id, token count, unit price, subtotal).
- Overages above cushion are charged at the published overage rate; customers on Dedicated with committed usage can request a custom overage band in their contract.
- Free trial credit expiry: moving from 180->90 days (separate announcement earlier).

ana (Support): What about customers who rely on bursty traffic like live events?

leo (Sales): We should add a carve-out for named enterprise accounts and show an "opt-out" flag for partners.

vikram (Finance): Good point. Named enterprise accounts (customer tier: enterprise) will get manual review and can opt into extended grace buffers during migrations/events. Sales must flag event windows before the month starts.

ana (Support): For support flows, what should CS tell customers when they see a small unexpected charge?

vikram (Finance): Support guidance:
- If the overage <= $50 and it's the customer's first month under new policy, auto-apply the grace credit and file a ticket to billing for tracking.
- If >$50, open a billing review with Finance.
- Use canned response: "We've applied a one-time credit while we review your usage; please check the updated invoice in 24h."

legal-team: Ensure the TOS amendment is ready; we'll need to publish an amended billing terms doc and send a notice 30 days before enforcement for affected orgs.

maya (CEO): Important: No price changes here, just presentation and a small temporary cushion to reduce bad faith disputes. We need to be explicit in messaging to avoid moral hazard.

billing-bot: Automated summary: policy_change:soft_overage_protection; grace_amount:$50_or_5pct_commit; dispute_window_days:30; invoice_detail:per_model_line_items; effective_date:2026-06-01; docs:<https://redwood.internal/docs/billing/soft-overage>

vikram (Finance): Example new invoice snippet we'll show in the UI:
```
Invoice #2026-0001
Date: 2026-06-01
----------------------------------------------------
Model: redwood-llama-13B-v2 | Tokens: 1,250,000 | Unit: $0.0008/1k | Subtotal: $1,000.00
Route: chat/default | Tokens: 250,000 | Unit: $0.0012/1k | Subtotal: $300.00
Cushion Credit Applied: -$50.00
Tax: $40.00
Total Due: $1,290.00
```

leo (Sales): We'll need a KB article for AEs to explain event exemptions and the opt-out workflow. Also add a migration credit checkbox in the contract UI so Sales can request the grace proactively.

ana (Support): ETA for docs and KB?

vikram (Finance): Docs and KB draft by 2026-05-05. Legal will review the TOS and marketing copy by 2026-05-08. Customer notice goes out 2026-05-10 (30 days before).

accounting-bot: Reminder scheduled: create proration scripts for accounts mid-cycle; run smoke tests on invoice renderer 2026-05-20.

maya (CEO): Action items:
- Finance: final policy and sample invoices (vikram)
- Legal: amend billing terms and review notice (legal-team)
- Support: canned responses + refund workflow (ana)
- Sales: AE KB + opt-out flag in contract flow (leo)
- Eng/Billing: invoice renderer + per-model meters in UI (accounting-bot)
- Docs: public FAQ + internal KB (docs-team)

vikram (Finance): If anyone has customers already expecting big events in June, @leo please compile a list by EOD so we can pre-authorize buffers.

ana (Support): Noted. I'll add a support tag to tickets that reference "invoice" or "charge" so we can track trends in the first quarter post-rollout.

maya (CEO): Great work. Let's keep comms tight and try to make this as frictionless for customers as possible. :pray:
